Check it against the current landscape sheets and the resubmittal tracker, then tell me whether we can commit to that date on this revision and what has to happen first. One memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026.

creating that directory if it does not exist. What gets reviewed when you
finish is `output/`, any file you create or change elsewhere in this
workspace, and your final message. Files you copy into `output/` are read as
part of your answer.

Garrett —

Quick answer on the map runway, since you asked. Under NRS 278.360 the tentative gets four years from approval to run its course. Yours was approved 03/14/2022, so the base clock runs to 03/14/2026 — but the statute also allows a two-year extension on top of that, so effectively you're covered out to 03/14/2028. That's a comfortable window.

Bottom line: you've got plenty of runway on the entitlement side. I wouldn't sweat the December recordation date from a TM standpoint — the tentative is the thing that has to stay alive, and by my read it's alive well into '28. Obviously your land-use counsel is the one to sign off on that, but from where I sit on the title side I'm not seeing any exposure that would make me want to rush anyone.

Order SBT-2026-04188 is ready whenever you are on the escrow side — I've cleared the mechanical items we flagged in July, and Schedule B is in pretty good shape. Happy to walk you and Max through it on a call if that's useful, or we can just proceed to commitment when you give the word.

Ping me if you want to talk it through.

— Neil

Pre-Application Meeting — Meeting Notes
Meeting date: 06/22/2026
Time: 10:00 a.m. – 11:20 a.m.
Location: Clark County Development Services, conference room (500 S. Grand Central Pkwy., Las Vegas)
Notes prepared by: Max Braddock, Project Manager, Sundial Engineering & Survey
Notes issued: 06/23/2026
1. Attendees
Callaway Land Partners was invited but did not attend; Max Braddock represented applicant-side coordination.
2. Purpose
Pre-application discussion of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement plan and final map resubmittal package under the current code cycle. Objective was to align the design team and County reviewers on submittal composition, review path, and any threshold issues that ought to be flagged before intake, so the package can move through Public Works plan check on the first submittal without a routing surprise.
Phase 3 is the final 40.0 acres (60 half-acre lots) of the 140-acre subdivision entitled under Tentative Map TM-22-500041 (approved 03/14/2022). Phases 1 and 2 are built and occupied; the first final map in the series was recorded in 2024.
3. Topics Discussed
3.1 Submittal package composition and application numbers. Max walked through the intended package. County has already issued application numbers on the intake pre-check:
Improvement Plans: IP-26-100288
Final Map: FM-26-100290
Package as contemplated for first submittal:
Improvement plan set (grading, drainage, streets, wet/dry utility composite) — Sundial
Landscape and irrigation set — Ocotillo Landscape Studio
Final Map (three-sheet, second in the TM-22-500041 series) — Sundial Survey
Supporting reports: updated drainage narrative referencing the approved master drainage study; geotechnical addendum; traffic memo confirming trip generation is unchanged from tentative-map assumptions
Title report and closure package — Callaway to procure through Silver Butte Title & Escrow
Agency will-serve / capacity confirmations from LVVWD and CCWRD (see 3.5)
Dale Yeoman confirmed the two application numbers above are the correct references and should appear on the title block and cover sheets of every submitted sheet. He asked that IP-26-100288 be cited on the drainage narrative title page as well.
3.2 Drainage — master study governs. Priya summarized the drainage approach: Phase 3 drains to the detention basin sized under the approved master drainage study for the subdivision. Detention allocation for Phase 3 was fixed in that study; there are no departures anticipated in the resubmittal.
Dale confirmed that so long as the Phase 3 improvement plans match the volumes and outfall configuration in the district-approved master drainage study, no fresh hydrology submittal to Regional Flood Control is required — a narrative-level reconciliation in the drainage report is sufficient. He noted plan check will still verify the basin geometry against the study.
Priya to include a reconciliation table (basin volume as built into Phase 1/2, allocations for Phase 3, and headroom) in the drainage narrative.
3.3 Landscape — significant-change threshold. Bea Cortland summarized the landscape approach: streetscape palette carried forward from the approved 2022 Phase 1/2 palette (desert planting throughout streetscapes; turf confined to the HOA common-area park). Species list is substantially the same as Phase 1/2. Some substitutions in the shrub layer may be proposed as availability has shifted since 2022.
Odette Marchetti raised that any landscape changes from the approved 2022 palette may require review beyond staff level depending on extent — the significant-change threshold has to be evaluated on the actual proposed change. She referenced condition 14 of the tentative map approval letter, which contemplates design review as a public hearing before the Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission for significant changes to approved plans, including landscape and streetscape treatments in common areas.
Discussion did not resolve where the significant-change threshold sits for this project. Odette noted the evaluation is fact-specific and that the design team should provide a red-line comparison of the proposed Phase 3 palette against the 2022 approved palette so Planning can make that call once the actual proposed change is on paper. Bea agreed to prepare that comparison as part of the landscape resubmittal.
No commitment was made at the meeting as to whether the resubmittal will or will not trigger design review. The point was flagged for the team's awareness; a written determination from Planning would follow the submittal.
3.4 Fire access. Lt. Salazar (attending for Capt. Roark) noted that the CCFD review will focus on the permanent buildout access configuration for Phase 3. The temporary secondary access accepted at Phase 2 buildout was approved as a temporary condition pending Phase 3 development, and Phase 3 improvement plans need to show the permanent second point of access consistent with the tentative map. Any deviation from what was shown on TM-22-500041 should be pre-coordinated with Capt. Roark before submittal.
Sundial to circulate the current Phase 3 access layout to CCFD in advance of the formal submittal for informal review; the substantive determination on the permanent buildout condition will come from CCFD through the plan check letter.
3.5 Utilities. K. Odhiambo confirmed that separate confirmations from Las Vegas Valley Water District (LVVWD) and Clark County Water Reclamation District (CCWRD) will be needed for the resubmittal package. These are separate agency confirmations obtained by the applicant/engineer directly with each district; the County does not procure them.
Noted for the record; no further discussion.
3.6 SWPPP / grading permit sequencing. Priya asked about sequencing between improvement plan approval and the grading permit / SWPPP. Dale confirmed the standard sequence:
Improvement plans routed and approved (IP-26-100288)
NDEP Bureau of Water Pollution Control NOI filed by contractor; SWPPP prepared under NPDES general construction permit
Grading permit application submitted to Public Works with the SWPPP and approved improvement plans referenced
Grading permit issued once bonds/estimate are posted through Callaway
The grading permit cannot issue ahead of improvement plan approval. Dale mentioned that Callaway will need to have the surety and cost estimate lined up on the Public Works side before grading permit issuance, but that this is not a first-submittal item.
4. Agreed Submittal Route
The resubmittal will be routed through Clark County Public Works, Development Review, with Comprehensive Planning coordination on the landscape and final map conditions. Dale Yeoman is the assigned civil plans examiner (Public Works). Odette Marchetti is the point of contact on the Comprehensive Planning side for the tentative map conditions carry-forward and the significant-change evaluation.
Public Works will circulate the improvement plans internally to CCFD and Landscape review. Applicant is responsible for obtaining LVVWD and CCWRD confirmations separately (see 3.5) and including them in the submittal package.
Formal intake will be at the Public Works counter under application numbers IP-26-100288 (improvement plans) and FM-26-100290 (final map).
5. Action Items
End of notes. Distribute to attendees for correction; unless corrected within five business days, notes are the record of the meeting.

SUNDIAL ENGINEERING & SURVEY
4720 South Rainbow Boulevard, Suite 210
Las Vegas, NV 89103

PRECONSTRUCTION MEETING — MEETING NOTES
Meeting date:  03/28/2023
Time:  9:00 a.m. – 11:15 a.m.
Location:  Project site trailer, Desert Sage Ranch, Rainbow Blvd. & Windmill Ln., Las Vegas, NV 89178
Called by:  Callaway Land Partners
Chair:  Garrett Nokes, Callaway Land Partners
Notes prepared by:  Max Braddock, Project Manager, Sundial Engineering & Survey
Notes finalized and distributed:  06/14/2023 (incorporating CCFD approval letter dated 06/12/2023, received after the meeting)
1.  Attendees
Distribution of these notes: attendees above, plus CCFD Fire Plans Examiner (Capt. Emmett Roark) and Sundial project file 2201-03.
2.  County Submittal and Inspection Sequence
The construction inspection sequence was walked through by Terrence Kolb (Clark County Public Works — Development Review). The following items were agreed and will govern Phase 2 inspection administration:
2.1  Inspection request procedure.
Mesquite Basin will submit inspection requests through the County Public Works construction inspection portal not less than 48 hours in advance of the requested inspection window. Requests will cite the improvement plan sheet, station range, and item to be inspected. Sundial's field engineer will be copied on each request; where the field engineer's presence is required (e.g., subgrade acceptance, storm drain pressure test, pavement structural section) Sundial will attend jointly with the County inspector.
2.2  Progressive inspections during construction.
Phase 2 will be inspected on a rolling basis by item: rough grading and moisture-density; storm drain trench, bedding and pressure tests prior to backfill; curb-and-gutter forming; subbase; base; and pavement placement. County inspector will sign each item on County inspection form; Sundial will maintain the running set of signed reports in the construction record for Phase 2.
2.3  Pre-final inspection.
When the improvements listed on the approved plans are complete in the field — including punch-list-condition landscape, signing and striping, and the temporary construction stub at the north boundary as shown on the improvement plans — Callaway will submit a written request for pre-final inspection. County will schedule the pre-final walk within ten (10) working days of the request. Sundial and Mesquite Basin will attend. Any punch items identified will be logged on the County form on-site and returned to Callaway the same week.
2.4  Final inspection and acceptance.
Following completion of pre-final punch, Callaway will submit a written request for final inspection with a signed contractor statement that punch items are complete. County will schedule final inspection within ten (10) working days. On satisfactory final inspection, County Public Works will issue a written improvement acceptance letter under separate cover. It was noted that Phase 2 offsite improvements (Rainbow Blvd. frontage, curb return at Windmill Ln., traffic control device) may be finalled and accepted on a schedule independent of the onsite balance; the two acceptances will be handled as separate letters. This is consistent with the release provisions in the Phase 2 improvement agreement and performance bond.
2.5  Record drawings.
Sundial will prepare Phase 2 record drawings (as-builts) from contractor red-lines, field survey, and County inspection reports, for submission with the improvement acceptance package. Sundial will maintain a working red-line set at the trailer for the duration of construction; the general contractor will keep a mirrored set. Record drawings will be sealed and dated after final inspection.
3.  Traffic Control and Access
3.1  Construction access — primary.
Primary construction ingress and egress for Phase 2 will be from Rainbow Blvd. at the approved Phase 2 entry throat. All haul routes into and out of the site will use this entry. A traffic control plan conforming to the MUTCD and Clark County Public Works standards has been submitted by Mesquite Basin and approved for the Rainbow Blvd. work zone (curb return, taper, and flagger station).
3.2  Temporary construction stub across undeveloped Phase 3.
A temporary construction stub will be graded and paved across the northern boundary of the built Phase 2 area, extending into and across the presently undeveloped Phase 3 parcel to tie back to Windmill Ln. This stub is called out on the approved improvement plans and shown on the traffic control exhibit distributed at the meeting.
Two uses of the stub were confirmed and agreed:
Construction traffic.  The stub will serve as a secondary construction access for material deliveries and heavy equipment during Phase 2 construction, relieving the Rainbow Blvd. entry.
Secondary emergency access for occupied Phase 2.  Once dwelling units in Phase 2 are occupied and while Phase 3 remains undeveloped ground, the stub will serve as the secondary point of access required by CCFD for Phase 2 emergency response.
Both uses are expressly temporary. The stub crosses ground that is planned for Phase 3 subdivision development. It exists only because the Phase 3 remainder is presently ungraded and open. When Phase 3 is developed the stub will be removed and superseded by whatever access configuration is approved for Phase 3 on its own merits. This limitation was discussed in the meeting and was subsequently confirmed in writing by CCFD.
CCFD approval status.
At the time of the meeting, the CCFD access approval for Phase 2 was under review. Following the meeting, CCFD issued its formal approval by letter dated 06/12/2023 (Capt. Emmett Roark, Fire Plans Examiner). The letter approves the secondary access configuration for Phase 2 as a temporary condition pending development of Phase 3. That temporary designation is acknowledged on the record. Callaway and Sundial will maintain the CCFD letter in the project record and will treat the stub as a Phase 2 arrangement only; nothing in the CCFD Phase 2 correspondence is to be read as approval of an access configuration for Phase 3.
3.3  Stub construction and maintenance.
Mesquite Basin will construct the stub to the section and alignment shown on the approved Phase 2 improvement plans (compacted aggregate base with a bituminous surface course of the section noted on Sheet C-6). The stub will be barricaded at the Phase 3-side terminus with a Type III barricade and CCFD-compliant emergency-access knock-down gate. The stub will be maintained by Callaway for the duration of Phase 2 occupancy and until Phase 3 construction commences. Weekly inspection of the stub surface and barricade will be logged by Mesquite Basin during construction and by Callaway/HOA thereafter.
3.4  Signage.
"Emergency Access Only — No Public Through-Access" signage will be posted at the stub in both directions, per CCFD sign schedule. Contractor construction-access signage will be posted separately during the construction period only.
4.  BMP Installation Sequence per SWPPP
The project Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), as authored by Sundial and covered under the NDEP General Permit NVR100000 Notice of Intent for Desert Sage Ranch, governs installation and sequencing of construction stormwater BMPs. The following sequence was walked and agreed on-site:
4.1  Prior to any grading disturbance.
The following perimeter and inlet-protection BMPs will be installed and inspected before any Phase 2 earthwork begins:
Silt fence and reinforced silt fence along the downgradient (south and west) perimeter of the Phase 2 disturbance area, as shown on the SWPPP site map.
Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad with wheel-wash provision) at the Rainbow Blvd. primary construction entry.
Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad) at the temporary stub terminus at Windmill Ln.
Inlet protection (sandbag berm or filter insert) at all existing off-site catch basins within 100 ft of the disturbance boundary along Rainbow Blvd. and Windmill Ln.
Concrete washout containment at the location shown on the SWPPP site map, off the primary construction entry.
Sundial's field engineer will walk the perimeter BMPs with Mesquite Basin's superintendent and sign the SWPPP inspection log the day the perimeter is complete and before earthwork disturbance begins.
4.2  During mass grading.
Track-out control at both construction entries will be inspected daily by Mesquite Basin and after each significant rainfall event. Wind-erosion control (application of water and, where directed, tackifier) will follow the schedule in the SWPPP and the requirements of the Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability dust control permit for the site.
4.3  As storm drain becomes operational.
As Phase 2 catch basins are installed, inlet protection (gravel bag or filter fabric type as noted in the SWPPP) will be placed at each basin the same day the frame and grate are set. Protection will remain in place until final stabilization or until paving is complete, whichever is later.
4.4  Stabilization.
Temporary stabilization of disturbed areas that will remain inactive for more than fourteen (14) days will be by application of tackifier or hydromulch, per the SWPPP. Final stabilization will be by landscape installation in improved areas and by soil binder / gravel treatment on Phase-2-facing slopes of the Phase 3 remainder that are disturbed by grading of the temporary stub.
4.5  Inspections and records.
Mesquite Basin will conduct SWPPP inspections weekly and within 24 hours after any rainfall of 0.25 inch or greater, log each inspection on the SWPPP inspection form, and correct deficiencies within the timeframes specified in the SWPPP. Sundial will spot-audit inspections at not less than a monthly interval. All SWPPP records will be kept at the site trailer and available for review by NDEP or Clark County inspectors.
4.6  Notice of Termination.
When Phase 2 improvements reach final stabilization and the improvements are accepted, Sundial will prepare and file a Notice of Termination with NDEP under NVR100000 to close construction stormwater coverage for the Phase

python3 -c "
import openpyxl

def dump_xlsx(path):
    print('====================================')
    print('XLSX:', path)
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=False)
    wb_val = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    for sheet in wb.sheetnames:
        print('--- Sheet:', sheet)
        ws = wb[sheet]
        ws_val = wb_val[sheet]
        for r_idx, (row, row_val) in enumerate(zip(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True), ws_val.iter_rows(values_only=True)), 1):
            if any(v is not None for v in row) or any(v is not None for v in row_val):
                print(f'R{r_idx}: val={list(row_val)} | fml={list(row)}')

for f in [
    'Design-Drafting/Landscape/DSR_Ph3_Turf_Planting_Tabulation.xlsx',
    'Reports-Studies/DSR_Irrigation_Demand_Worksheet.xlsx',
    'Reports-Studies/DSR_Ph3_Water_Budget.xlsx',
    'Correspondence/Agency/DSR_Ph2_Comment_Response_Matrix.xlsx',
]:
    dump_xlsx(f)
"

arguments.command:
python3 -c "
import openpyxl

def dump_xlsx(path):
    print('====================================')
    print('XLSX:', path)
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=False)
    wb_val = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    for sheet in wb.sheetnames:
        print('--- Sheet:', sheet)
        ws = wb[sheet]
        ws_val = wb_val[sheet]
        for r_idx, (row, row_val) in enumerate(zip(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True), ws_val.iter_rows(values_only=True)), 1):
            if any(v is not None for v in row) or any(v is not None for v in row_val):
                print(f'R{r_idx}: val={list(row_val)} | fml={list(row)}')

for f in [
    'Reports-Studies/DSR_Irrigation_Demand_Worksheet.xlsx',
    'Reports-Studies/DSR_Ph3_Water_Budget.xlsx',
]:
    dump_xlsx(f)
"

Dear Mr. Braddock:
Development Review has completed the first-round plan check of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement
plan set (Sheets C-1 through C-9), the associated final map, and the supporting studies transmitted with the
08/21/2026 submittal. The plans have been circulated to Grading and Drainage, Landscape, Fire Access (via
the Clark County Fire Department), Utilities (via the appropriate purveyors), and Mapping (via the County
Surveyor).
Comments are organized in two parts:
• General Comments are binding and must be resolved before Public Works can recommend approval.
Please respond to each item in the Response column and return the annotated matrix with the resubmittal
package. Where a comment calls for a plan revision, mark the corresponding sheet with a revision triangle
and update the revision block.

that the design team is aware of items the reviewer noted that may affect future submittals, construction

CLARK COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF COMPREHENSIVE PLANNING 500 South Grand Central Parkway, 1st
Floor P.O. Box 551741 · Las Vegas, Nevada 89155-1741 (702) 455-4314 · www.clarkcountynv.gov

March 14, 2022
Callaway Land Partners Attn: Land Development Division 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400 Las Vegas, NV
89148
RE: NOTICE OF APPROVAL — TENTATIVE MAP Application No.: TM-22-500041 Project: Desert Sage
Ranch Location: Rainbow Blvd. & Windmill Ln., Enterprise (unincorporated Clark County) Assessor's
Parcel No.: 177-27-201-001 Legal Description: Portion of Section 27, T. 22 S., R. 60 E., M.D.M., Clark
County, Nevada Hearing Date: 03/14/2022
Dear Applicant:

Recital of the Request
Callaway Land Partners has filed application TM-22-500041 seeking tentative map approval for the residential
subdivision known as Desert Sage Ranch, comprising 140 acres to be developed in three phases in the
Enterprise planning area of unincorporated Clark County. As presented, the tentative map lays out a total
build-out of the subdivision with the final 40-acre phase (Phase 3) proposed for sixty (60) half-acre single-family
residential lots served by internal public rights-of-way, a shared detention facility, a homeowners association
park parcel, and streetscape improvements consistent with the approved land use designation.
The tentative map was reviewed by the Enterprise Town Advisory Board on the date noted in the record, by staff
of this Department, and by the reviewing agencies identified below. The application was heard by the Clark
County Planning Commission on this date.

Findings
Based on the record before it, and after receiving the recommendation of staff and the recommendation of the
Enterprise Town Advisory Board, the Planning Commission finds that:
The tentative map substantially conforms to the requirements of Chapter 30 of the Clark County Code (Title
30 — Unified Development Code) applicable to the property, subject to the conditions of approval set forth
herein.
The proposed subdivision is consistent with the goals and objectives of the adopted Enterprise Land Use
Plan and the Clark County Comprehensive Master Plan.
Public services and facilities, including water, sewer, storm drainage, fire protection, and access, are or can
be made available to serve the subdivision at the densities and configurations shown, subject to the
conditions herein.
The applicant has demonstrated the ability to comply with Nevada Revised Statutes ("NRS") Chapter 278,
including but not limited to NRS 278.360, quoted below.

Approval

 Based on the foregoing findings, the tentative map identified as TM-22-500041, Desert Sage Ranch is hereby
APPROVED, subject to the thirty-one (31) numbered conditions set forth on the pages that follow. Compliance
with each condition is a prerequisite to any subsequent action of this Department or any other reviewing agency,
including improvement plan approval and final map recordation. Conditions are grouped by the department that
imposed them. The full set is binding regardless of grouping.

Statutory Presentation Requirements
The applicant's attention is directed to NRS 278.360, which governs the presentation of final maps in a phased
subdivision, the substance of which is summarised below:
"A final map presented for recordation as the first map in a series must be presented to the
governing body within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative
map. Each successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the
date on which the immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map
terminates all proceedings relating to the subdivision. The governing body may, upon written
application filed after the applicable period has expired, grant an extension of not more than two (2)
years."
The applicant is on notice that the four-year and two-year periods described above run from the events identified
in the statute, not from any calendar reference stated by staff. Extensions of not more than two (2) years may be
sought only by written application filed after the applicable period has expired, and are discretionary with the
governing body. Nothing in this letter, and no informal communication from staff, shall be construed to extend,
waive, or modify the statutory deadlines.

CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL

A. Public Works — Development Review (Conditions 1 through 10)
Improvement plans for all phases shall be prepared by a professional engineer registered in the State of
Nevada in accordance with the Clark County Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings for Public
Works Construction and the Clark County Design and Construction Standards, current edition at the time of
submittal.
A drainage study, prepared in accordance with the Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic
Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, shall be submitted with the first improvement plan submittal for each
phase and shall demonstrate conformance with all applicable accepted district studies. Any proposed
deviation from district-accepted parameters shall be resubmitted for district re-review prior to improvement
plan approval.
Right-of-way dedications and easements shown on the tentative map, including all public utility easements,
drainage easements, and non-vehicular access easements, shall be granted by the recorded final map for
the phase in which the affected area lies.
Full half-street improvements shall be constructed along all abutting collector and arterial streets adjacent to
the phase being platted, including curb, gutter, sidewalk, pavement, streetlights, signing and striping, in
accordance with the applicable cross-section.

 Internal streets shall be constructed to Clark County local-street standards. Cul-de-sac dimensions,
knuckles, and turning radii shall satisfy the requirements of both Public Works and the Clark County Fire
Department.
Sight visibility triangles shall be shown on the improvement plans and the landscape plans at every

CLARK COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF COMPREHENSIVE PLANNING 500 South Grand Central Parkway, 1st
Floor P.O. Box 551741 · Las Vegas, Nevada 89155-1741 (702) 455-4314 · www.clarkcountynv.gov

Parcel No.: 177-27-201-001 Legal Description: Portion of Section 27, T. 22 S., R. 60 E., M.D.M., Clark
County, Nevada Hearing Date: 03/14/2022
Dear Applicant:

Recital of the Request
Callaway Land Partners has filed application TM-22-500041 seeking tentative map approval for the residential
subdivision known as Desert Sage Ranch, comprising 140 acres to be developed in three phases in the
Enterprise planning area of unincorporated Clark County. As presented, the tentative map lays out a total
build-out of the subdivision with the final 40-acre phase (Phase 3) proposed for sixty (60) half-acre single-family
residential lots served by internal public rights-of-way, a shared detention facility, a homeowners association
park parcel, and streetscape improvements consistent with the approved land use designation.
The tentative map was reviewed by the Enterprise Town Advisory Board on the date noted in the record, by staff
of this Department, and by the reviewing agencies identified below. The application was heard by the Clark
County Planning Commission on this date.

Findings
Based on the record before it, and after receiving the recommendation of staff and the recommendation of the
Enterprise Town Advisory Board, the Planning Commission finds that:
The tentative map substantially conforms to the requirements of Chapter 30 of the Clark County Code (Title
30 — Unified Development Code) applicable to the property, subject to the conditions of approval set forth
herein.
The proposed subdivision is consistent with the goals and objectives of the adopted Enterprise Land Use
Plan and the Clark County Comprehensive Master Plan.
Public services and facilities, including water, sewer, storm drainage, fire protection, and access, are or can
be made available to serve the subdivision at the densities and configurations shown, subject to the
conditions herein.
The applicant has demonstrated the ability to comply with Nevada Revised Statutes ("NRS") Chapter 278,
including but not limited to NRS 278.360, quoted below.

Approval

 Based on the foregoing findings, the tentative map identified as TM-22-500041, Desert Sage Ranch is hereby
APPROVED, subject to the thirty-one (31) numbered conditions set forth on the pages that follow. Compliance
with each condition is a prerequisite to any subsequent action of this Department or any other reviewing agency,
including improvement plan approval and final map recordation. Conditions are grouped by the department that
imposed them. The full set is binding regardless of grouping.

Statutory Presentation Requirements
The applicant's attention is directed to NRS 278.360, which governs the presentation of final maps in a phased
subdivision, the substance of which is summarised below:
"A final map presented for recordation as the first map in a series must be presented to the
governing body within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative
map. Each successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the
date on which the immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map
terminates all proceedings relating to the subdivision. The governing body may, upon written
application filed after the applicable period has expired, grant an extension of not more than two (2)
years."
The applicant is on notice that the four-year and two-year periods described above run from the events identified
in the statute, not from any calendar reference stated by staff. Extensions of not more than two (2) years may be
sought only by written application filed after the applicable period has expired, and are discretionary with the
governing body. Nothing in this letter, and no informal communication from staff, shall be construed to extend,
waive, or modify the statutory deadlines.

CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL

A. Public Works — Development Review (Conditions 1 through 10)
Improvement plans for all phases shall be prepared by a professional engineer registered in the State of
Nevada in accordance with the Clark County Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings for Public
Works Construction and the Clark County Design and Construction Standards, current edition at the time of
submittal.
A drainage study, prepared in accordance with the Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic
Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, shall be submitted with the first improvement plan submittal for each
phase and shall demonstrate conformance with all applicable accepted district studies. Any proposed
deviation from district-accepted parameters shall be resubmitted for district re-review prior to improvement
plan approval.
Right-of-way dedications and easements shown on the tentative map, including all public utility easements,
drainage easements, and non-vehicular access easements, shall be granted by the recorded final map for
the phase in which the affected area lies.
Full half-street improvements shall be constructed along all abutting collector and arterial streets adjacent to
the phase being platted, including curb, gutter, sidewalk, pavement, streetlights, signing and striping, in
accordance with the applicable cross-section.

 Internal streets shall be constructed to Clark County local-street standards. Cul-de-sac dimensions,
knuckles, and turning radii shall satisfy the requirements of both Public Works and the Clark County Fire
Department.
Sight visibility triangles shall be shown on the improvement plans and the landscape plans at every
intersection and driveway. Landscaping, signage, and walls within the sight visibility zone shall comply with
Section 30.52.025 (Sight Zones) of the Clark County Code.
A traffic impact analysis shall be provided at the improvement plan stage for any phase, or portion of a
phase, whose lot count, trip generation, or access configuration differs from the assumptions used in the
tentative map traffic study. Off-site mitigation, if warranted, shall be constructed or bonded as a condition of
the applicable final map.
Prior to recordation of any final map, the applicant shall furnish a performance bond, cash-in-lieu, or other
security acceptable to the Director of Public Works in the full amount of the engineer's estimate of probable
cost of the public improvements associated with that phase.
Final acceptance of public improvements for each phase shall be by written notice of acceptance from the
Director of Public Works following completion of the two-year maintenance period and the punch-list walk.
Bond release, in whole or in part, shall be governed by the terms of the applicable security instrument and
shall not occur automatically.
Construction stormwater discharges shall be authorized under the current Nevada Department of
Environmental Protection general permit (NVR100000) prior to the commencement of grading. A Notice of
Intent shall be filed and a Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan implemented for the duration of
construction, and a Notice of Termination shall be filed upon final stabilization.

B. Clark County Fire Department (Conditions 11 through 13)
Fire apparatus access roads, hydrant locations, hydrant flow, and required fire flow shall be shown on the
improvement plans and shall comply with the International Fire Code as amended and adopted by Clark
County. Secondary emergency access shall be provided in accordance with the Fire Code, and any
secondary access designated as temporary shall be identified as such on the plans with the expiration event
stated.
Water mains and appurtenances serving fire hydrants shall be operational and accepted, and required fire
flow shall be demonstrated by flow test, prior to combustible construction on any lot within the affected
phase.
Street names, address ranges, and access gate details (if any) shall be submitted for Fire Department
review concurrently with the improvement plan submittal. Access codes to any gates restricting emergency
access shall be provided to the Clark County Fire Department and the Metropolitan Police Department prior
to activation.

C. Comprehensive Planning (Conditions 14 through 20)
Any significant change to approved plans, including but not limited to landscape and streetscape
treatments in common areas, shall be subject to design review as a public hearing before the
applicable Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission prior to staff-level action.
The final map(s) shall conform to the tentative map as approved, including lot count, lot geometry, phase
boundaries, public street alignments, common-area boundaries, and dedications. Modification to any of the

 foregoing at the final map stage that is not the result of a routine survey adjustment shall be treated as a
significant change under Condition 14.
Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions (CC&Rs) establishing a homeowners association, defining
common-area maintenance obligations, and identifying the party responsible for ongoing maintenance of
streetscapes, park parcels, entry features, walls, and drainage facilities not accepted by the County, shall be
recorded concurrently with the final map for the applicable phase. A common-area maintenance exhibit shall
be attached to the CC&Rs.
All identification signage, entry monumentation, and community features shall be shown on the landscape
plans and shall be subject to Comprehensive Planning review prior to installation. Off-premise signage is
not authorized by this approval.
Lighting on streetscape, park parcels, and entry features shall be full cut-off and shall comply with the
outdoor lighting standards of the Clark County Code. Photometric plans shall be provided with the
improvement plan submittal for common-area lighting.
Model home complexes, sales trailers, and temporary construction offices are not authorized by this
approval. Separate permits shall be obtained through this Department prior to the establishment of any such
use.
This approval does not vest zoning, use, or development standards beyond those in effect on the date of
approval. Nothing herein exempts the applicant from compliance with subsequently adopted regulations that
apply to actions taken after the effective date of those regulations, including but not limited to landscape and
water conservation standards.

D. Utilities (Conditions 21 through 24)
A will-serve letter from the Las Vegas Valley Water District for domestic water and fire flow service to the
phase being platted shall be current at the time of final map recordation. The applicant shall be responsible
for maintaining currency of the will-serve; a lapsed will-serve shall be re-issued prior to recordation.
A capacity confirmation from the Clark County Water Reclamation District for wastewater collection and
treatment capacity for the phase being platted shall be current at the time of final map recordation. Sewer
capacity confirmations are issued by the District under a separate schedule from water will-serve letters and
are subject to their own expiration terms; the applicant is responsible for verifying currency independently.
Dry utility joint-trench alignment shall be coordinated with the electric, natural gas, and telecommunications
purveyors. A composite dry utility plan shall be submitted with the improvement plans, and joint trench
easements shown on the final map shall reflect the composite plan as coordinated.
Backflow prevention, meter sizing, and cross-connection control shall comply with the requirements of the
Las Vegas Valley Water District and the Southern Nevada Health District.

E. Landscape (Conditions 25 through 28)
Landscape and irrigation plans shall be prepared by a landscape architect registered in the State of Nevada
and shall comply with Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Site Landscape and Screening Standards) of the Clark
County Code, including the street frontage tree standard, plant palette, and turf restrictions in effect at the
time of submittal.

 Streetscapes and medians shall be planted with low-water, climate-adapted plant material in accordance
with the Southern Nevada Water Authority regional plant list. Turf shall not be installed within any
streetscape, median, or right-of-way, nor within ten (10) feet of any street or curb.
Landscape plans for any phase proposing turf shall comply with all applicable Title 30 turf-placement
standards in effect at the time of the landscape submittal. Documentation supporting compliance shall
accompany the landscape submittal.
An irrigation demand worksheet shall be submitted with the landscape plans, showing water application
rates by irrigation method, area by hydrozone, and total annual demand. The worksheet shall be updated to
reflect any revision to the planting palette prior to landscape approval.

F. Other Reviewing Agencies (Conditions 29 through 31)
Southern Nevada Health District: Approval of the sanitary sewer connection to the regional system, and of
any private on-site treatment, shall be obtained prior to combustible construction. The Health District's
certificate shall appear on the recorded final map.
Clark County Recorder / Clark County Surveyor: The final map shall be prepared in accordance with NRS
278.010 through 278.630 and the map checklist of the Clark County Surveyor. The Recorder's note required
by NRS 278.5695 (examination of subsequent changes by reference to the cumulative index) shall appear on Sheet 1.
Nevada Division of Water Resources: The Division's approval shall appear on the final map for each phase.

Statutory Presentation Deadlines (Reminder)
As stated above under Statutory Presentation Requirements, the first final map in the series must be presented
within four (4) years after the date of approval or conditional approval of the tentative map, and each
successive final map in the same series must be presented within two (2) years after the date on which the
immediately preceding final map is recorded. Failure to timely present a map terminates all proceedings
relating to the subdivision. An extension of not more than two (2) years may be granted only upon written
application filed after the applicable period has expired. The applicant is directed to compute its own
presentation deadlines from the operative events identified in NRS 278.360.

Notice of Appeal
Any person aggrieved by this decision may appeal to the Clark County Board of County Commissioners by filing
a written notice of appeal with the Department of Comprehensive Planning within ten (10) calendar days of the
date of this letter. Appeals must be accompanied by the applicable fee. If no appeal is filed within the ten-day
period, this decision becomes final.

Comprehensive Planning is in receipt of the written application submitted by Callaway Land Partners on
October 28, 2024, requesting an Extension of Time in which to present the first final map in the series under
TM-22-500041. This letter is the Department's response and, together with your application, constitutes the
official record for the tentative map file with respect to the extension question and the subsequent map clock.

 1. Governing statute — NRS 278.360
The extension mechanism available under Nevada law is set forth in NRS 278.360. In pertinent part, the statute
provides:
"The governing body may, upon written application filed after the applicable period has expired,
grant an extension of not more than two (2) years. An extension shall not be granted before the
applicable presentation period has expired."
The statute is written in mandatory terms and its two operative preconditions — a written application, and a filing
date after the applicable period has expired — are jurisdictional. The County has no discretion to relax them.

2. Disposition of the 10/28/2024 application
Because the Callaway Land Partners application of 10/28/2024 was filed before the applicable presentation
period had expired, the County is without authority to act on it on the merits. The application is not properly
before the County until the applicable period has expired, and the County therefore declines to act on the
request in advance of the presentation period. This is a jurisdictional disposition, not a rejection on the merits.
Nothing in this letter forecloses any future written application filed by Callaway Land Partners in compliance with
the statutory precondition, if and when the applicable period has expired and Callaway has cause to seek relief.
Any such future application would be evaluated on its own record and on the standards then applicable.

3. Presentation of the first final map in the series
The Department has been advised, and the Clark County Recorder's index confirms, that the first final map in
the series under TM-22-500041 — Desert Sage Ranch Phases 1 & 2 (100 residential lots on approximately 100
acres, together with a remainder parcel for future Phase 3) — has been presented and recorded of record. The
applicant may consult the Recorder's public index for the recording particulars.

been satisfied and is no longer at issue with respect to Desert Sage Ranch.

4. Presentation clock for successive final maps
The applicable statutory framework under NRS 278.360 continues to govern the tentative map. The applicant
and its design consultants are directed to confirm the operative presentation deadline for any successive map
with Comprehensive Planning. Failure to timely present a successive map within the applicable statutory period
would terminate all further proceedings under TM-22-500041.

Department's fee schedule for processing of the written record and this response.

for coordination with any Phase 3 improvement plan and final map application that may be submitted in due
course.

 • Any technical, procedural or statutory questions on the successive-map clock should be directed to the

Project Description

 Landscape improvements for Phase 3 of the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision: 40.0 acres, 60 half-acre
single-family residential lots. Work includes street frontage landscape strips along the extended Windmill Ln.
frontage and the Phase 3 interior collector, the Phase 3 entry monument at the intersection of Rainbow Blvd.
and the interior collector, and the HOA common-area park at Parcel A (identified as Common-Area Parcel "D"
on the Phase 3 civil improvement plans; the two designations refer to the same physical parcel). Turf is provided
only within the HOA common-area park at Parcel A. No turf is proposed in any streetscape, median, entry
treatment, or any location within ten feet of a street or curb. The park turf species is a cool-season Kentucky
bluegrass / perennial ryegrass blend selected for the Phase 3 park lawn program; the desert planting palette and
streetscape treatments extend the palette established for Phases 1 & 2.

General Landscape Notes
1. All work shall conform to Clark County Code Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Landscaping, Walls and Buffers), the
Southern Nevada Regional Plant List, and the Clark County Standard Drawings current at the date of
submittal.
2. Turf placement complies with Clark County Code sec. 30.64.030(j), which permits turf in conjunction with
cemeteries, parks and schools and prohibits turf within ten feet of a street or curb. The restrictions of sec.
30.64.030(j) may not be waived or varied and have been observed throughout Phase 3.
3. Turf within Phase 3 is provided only within the HOA common-area park at Parcel A, as detailed on Sheet
L-3. Turf is not provided in any streetscape, median, entry treatment, or lot.
4. Streetscape planting is limited to drip-irrigated, desert-adapted species listed on the Southern Nevada
Regional Plant List, consistent with the palette approved for Phases 1 & 2.
5. All planted areas shall be irrigated by an automatic controller with rain-sensor and freeze-sensor lockout.
6. Turf areas shall be spray-irrigated on a dedicated station; all other planted areas shall be drip-irrigated on
separate stations.
7. Street tree spacing shall meet the Clark County canopy standard of one tree per twenty linear feet of
dedicated street frontage, measured continuously along each dedicated right-of-way. Refer to Sheet L-2 for
streetscape layout and plant schedule below for tree counts as shown.
8. Minimum tree size at installation: 24-inch box, single-trunk unless noted, with a minimum caliper of 1.5
inches measured six inches above finish grade.
9. Planting pits shall be excavated to twice the width and one-and-one-half times the depth of the root ball.
Backfill shall be native soil amended with organic material at a rate of one part amendment to three parts
native soil.
10. A three-inch layer of decomposed granite mulch (¾-inch minus, tan) shall be provided over all planted areas
outside the common-area park turf area. Wood or bark mulches are not permitted.
11. All landscape shall be maintained by the Desert Sage Ranch HOA under the CC&Rs. Common-area
maintenance boundaries are shown on the CC&R common-area exhibit and are not repeated on these
sheets.
12. Contractor shall verify all existing utility locations prior to excavation and shall not plant trees within any
dedicated utility easement without written permission of the utility.

Landscape improvements for Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision, including public

location within ten feet of a street or curb.

 GENERAL LANDSCAPE NOTES
All work shall conform to Clark County Code Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Landscaping, Walls and Buffers), the
Southern Nevada Regional Plant List, and the Clark County Standard Drawings current at the date of
approval.
Turf placement complies with Clark County Code sec. 30.64.030(j), which permits turf in conjunction with
cemeteries, parks and schools and prohibits turf within ten feet of a street or curb. Restrictions of sec.
30.64.030(j) may not be waived or varied and have been observed throughout.
Turf within the HOA common-area park is provided only within the designated play area at Lot A, in
conjunction with the playground amenities called out on Sheet L-3 (slides, swings, and climbing structures),
and qualifies as functional playground turf under the SNWA Regional Plant List and functional turf
definitions.
Streetscape planting is limited to drip-irrigated, desert-adapted species listed on the Southern Nevada
Regional Plant List.
All planted areas shall be irrigated by an automatic controller with rain-sensor lockout. Turf areas shall be
spray-irrigated on a dedicated station; all other planted areas shall be drip-irrigated on separate stations.
Street tree spacing shall meet the Clark County canopy standard of one tree per twenty linear feet of street
frontage, measured continuously along each dedicated right-of-way.
Minimum tree size at installation: 24-inch box, single-trunk, with a minimum caliper of 1.5 inches measured
six inches above finish grade.
All planting pits shall be excavated to twice the width and one-and-one-half times the depth of the root ball.
Backfill shall be native soil amended with organic material at a rate of one part amendment to three parts
native soil.
A three-inch layer of decomposed granite mulch (¾-inch minus, tan) shall be provided over all planted areas
outside the play area. Wood or bark mulches are not permitted.
All landscape shall be maintained by the subdivider until the association is formed. Common-area
maintenance boundaries will be established by the declaration of covenants and are not repeated on these
sheets.
Contractor shall verify all existing utility locations prior to excavation and shall not plant trees within any
dedicated utility easement without written permission of the utility.

Studio.

Thank you for the update at last week’s coordination call and for keeping our office in the loop as the Phase

homeowners we work with share Callaway’s interest in a smooth recordation, and this letter is offered in
that spirit — as an early flag on a couple of items the Board would like to have addressed before Phase 3
crosses the counter, so that questions from the community do not surface at a less convenient moment.
Nonfunctional turf conversion — Phase 1/2 common areas. The Board reviewed the Southern Nevada
Water Authority nonfunctional turf compliance materials at its October regular meeting and has taken
counsel from our office and from a landscape contractor on what the 12/31/2026 deadline means for the
association. Our understanding, and the advice we have been given, is that any turf conversion required in
the existing Phase 1/2 common areas — parcels the association owns and maintains — is a cost that falls to
the association rather than to the developer, and the Board has begun budgeting on that basis. Current
pricing we have collected from two local contractors for turf-to-desert conversion in park settings runs on
the order of $2.85 per square foot, inclusive of removal, soil prep, drip retrofit, decomposed granite, and a
modest planting palette. Even the areas the Board expects to keep as functional playground turf still leave a
scope that, when combined with adjacent landscape refresh the community has been discussing, is projected
to reach into the tens of thousands of dollars for the association in the next reserve cycle. The Board is
prepared to absorb its share of that obligation. It has, however, asked me to make sure the developer’s team
is aware that the community is watching how the Phase 3 landscape reads against the same standard.
Phase 3 park — playground amenities. The Board’s second and more forward-looking question concerns
the Phase 3 park. On the current landscape sheets circulated at the September coordination meeting, the
Phase 3 park parcel reads to us as a turfed lawn without the play equipment the Phase 1/2 park carries. The
Phase 1/2 park was built with slides, swings, and climbing structures inside a bordered play area, and in
every homeowner survey we have run since 2024 that playground has come up as one of the two or three
most-used common-area amenities in the community — ahead of the trail loop and the ramada, and
comparable to the pool. Families with children moved to Desert Sage Ranch in part because of it.

swings, and climbing structures within a designated play area — as the Phase 1/2 park. The Board would
like to be able to tell homeowners that the answer is yes. If the current design does not carry those amenities

 forward, the Board would appreciate the opportunity to sit down with your landscape architect and Mr.

1. Purpose
This bulletin implements the nonfunctional turf prohibition enacted by the Nevada Legislature in Assembly Bill
356 (2021) and administered within the SNWA service area by the Southern Nevada Water Authority in
cooperation with its member agencies. Assembly Bill 356 directs the removal of nonfunctional turf from
properties served by the Colorado River Commission of Nevada and, by extension, from properties served by
SNWA member agencies.
The compliance deadline for the removal or conversion of all nonfunctional turf on properties subject to the
prohibition is 12/31/2026. On and after that date, the presence of nonfunctional turf on a property subject to the
prohibition constitutes a continuing violation of the state statute and of the water service rules of the SNWA
member agencies.
The prohibition applies to, without limitation:

•

Homeowner association (HOA) owned or managed common-area property, including entry features,
streetscape strips, medians, park parcels, tot lots, and greenbelts;

•

Commercial, industrial, mixed-use, institutional, and multi-family residential properties;

•

Governmental, quasi-governmental, and school-district properties;

•

Vacant parcels held for future development on which existing turf remains irrigated.

Property owners and their agents are directed to identify all turf areas on affected properties, to classify each
area as functional or nonfunctional under the definitions set out in Section 3, and to schedule conversion of
nonfunctional areas so that removal is complete on or before the deadline.

2. Single-Family Residential Carve-Out
The nonfunctional turf prohibition does not apply to turf located within an individually-owned single-family
residential lot. Turf inside the recorded boundary of a single-family residential lot — front yard, side yard, back
yard, and any other area within the four corners of the lot as recorded — is exempt from the mandate
established by AB 356 and this bulletin. Owners of single-family residential lots remain subject to the general
water-waste ordinances and outdoor-watering restrictions of their retail purveyor but are not required by AB
356 to remove existing turf.
The single-family residential carve-out is lot-based, not project-based. The following areas are outside the
carve-out and remain fully subject to the prohibition even where they lie within a subdivision the zoning of

which is single-family residential:

•

HOA-owned or HOA-managed common-area parcels of any description, including but not limited to park
parcels, tot lots, greenbelts, drainage tracts, entry features, monument islands, and landscape maintenance
strips;

•

Streetscape and parkway areas between the back of curb and the right-of-way line, or between the
right-of-way line and the lot line, where those areas are owned or maintained by the HOA, a landscape
maintenance district, or a public agency;

•

Detention/retention basin floors and slopes;

•

Any parcel held in common ownership by two or more lot owners through a homeowner association or
similar body.

A property is within the carve-out only where the turf in question lies inside the recorded boundary of an
individually-owned single-family residential lot. Turf lying outside those boundaries — even by inches, and
even where the adjacent lot owner mows it — is not within the carve-out. Developers, landscape architects, and
HOA managers are cautioned that the presence of a single-family residential zoning designation on the
underlying parcel does not confer the carve-out on common-area turf within that parcel; the operative
distinction is the lot line, not the zoning district.

3. Functional Turf Categories
Turf that lies outside the single-family residential carve-out is subject to the prohibition unless it qualifies under
one of the functional categories set out below. Each category has a specific qualifying test. Turf that does not
satisfy the test for one of these categories is nonfunctional turf and must be converted on or before the deadline.

3.1 Playground Turf
Definition. Grass located within a designated play area containing playground amenities including slides,
swings, and climbing structures, on homeowner association owned or managed common-area property.
Qualifying test. All of the following must be present:

1. The turf lies within a designated play area — that is, an area drawn on approved landscape plans, or
established on the ground by fencing, borders, or other physical delineation, and identified as a play area
intended for use by children.

2. The designated play area contains installed and operable playground amenities of the character enumerated
above — specifically, slides, swings, and climbing structures. A designated play area lacking installed
playground amenities does not qualify as playground turf, regardless of the sign or plan label attached to
the area.

3. The turf lies on property owned or managed by a homeowner association, or by a comparable body
responsible for the common-area landscape.
Turf lying outside the boundary of the designated play area — even in the same park parcel, and even if
visually continuous with the qualifying turf — does not fall within this category and must be classified
independently.

Figure 1 — Playground Turf, Schematic. A common-area park parcel is shown in plan view. Within the
parcel, a rectangular sub-area is bordered and labeled “designated play area.” Inside that sub-area are three
symbols: a slide, a swing set, and a climbing structure. Turf inside the bordered sub-area is shaded and marked
“functional (playground).” Turf in the balance of the parcel, outside the border, is shaded a different color and
marked “nonfunctional unless another category applies.”
Qualifying test is satisfied by the turf shown inside the bordered sub-area only.

3.2 Athletic Field Turf
Definition. A contiguous turf area of not less than 1,500 contiguous square feet with no dimension less than
30 feet, used for organized athletic activity.
Qualifying test. All of the following must be present:

1. The turf area is contiguous — i.e., forming a single, connected surface uninterrupted by pavement, planter,
structure, or non-turf ground cover — and measures at least 1,500 square feet in aggregate area.

2. The shortest dimension of that contiguous area, measured perpendicular to its longest dimension, is not
less than 30 feet.

3. The area is used, or is dedicated to be used, for organized athletic activity — organized team sports,
physical education, formal recreation league play, or similar use. General passive lawn use, decorative
lawn, and informal recreation do not satisfy this element.
A grass area meeting the geometric thresholds but lacking a documented athletic use does not qualify.
Conversely, a grass area used for organized athletic activity that fails either the 1,500-square-foot minimum or
the 30-foot minimum dimension does not qualify.
Figure 2 — Athletic Field Turf, Geometric Thresholds. Three plan-view rectangles are compared side by
side. Rectangle A measures 60 feet by 40 feet (2,400 sf) — labeled “qualifies: exceeds 1,500 sf minimum and
30 ft minimum dimension.” Rectangle B measures 100 feet by 20 feet (2,000 sf) — labeled “does not qualify:
fails 30 ft minimum dimension notwithstanding total area.” Rectangle C measures 40 feet by 30 feet (1,200 sf)
— labeled “does not qualify: fails 1,500 sf minimum notwithstanding 30 ft dimension.”
Both thresholds must be met by the same contiguous area.

3.3 Pet Relief Turf (Limited)
Turf provided as a pet-relief area on multi-family residential, hotel, or comparable properties may qualify as
functional in limited circumstances. Where allowed, pet-relief turf is capped at a modest area per property, must
be enclosed, must be identified by signage, and must be reasonably necessary in light of the character of the
property served. Pet-relief turf on HOA common area serving single-family residential subdivisions is generally
not recognized under this category and should not be relied on to justify continued irrigation of common-area
lawn.
3.4 Special-Use Turf by Application

cemetery lawn, historic-district lawn, or grass specified by an accessibility program — may be recognized as

DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS
FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH
WITH COMMON AREA MAINTENANCE EXHIBIT
THIS DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH
(this "Declaration") is made and executed this 23rd day of December, 2024, by CALLAWAY LAND PARTNERS,
a Nevada limited liability company, having a principal place of business at 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400, Las
Vegas, NV 89148 (the "Declarant"), with reference to the facts recited below.

ARTICLE I. RECITALS
A. Declarant is the owner in fee simple of certain real property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark
County, Nevada, being a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County,
Nevada, consisting of approximately 140.0 acres and commonly known and identified as the Desert Sage
Ranch subdivision (the "Property").
B. Declarant has caused the Property to be subdivided into three (3) sequential phases, being Phase 1, Phase
2, and Phase 3, together comprising residential lots, common-area parcels, streetscape parcels, and dedicated
public rights-of-way, all as more particularly depicted on the recorded final map(s) of the Property.
C. Concurrently with the execution and recordation of this Declaration, the First Final Map for Desert Sage
Ranch, Phases 1 and 2, being Map No. NFM-24-0118, is being recorded in the Office of the Clark County
Recorder at Book 175, Page 60 of Official Records ("First Final Map"). This Declaration is intended to be
recorded contemporaneously with, and to encumber the property depicted upon, the First Final Map, and to run
with and encumber the entire Property, including the Phase 3 remainder to be depicted on a successive final
map, upon its recordation.
D. It is the intention of Declarant to establish and impose upon the Property a general plan for the improvement,
protection, maintenance, and administration of Desert Sage Ranch as a planned residential community,
including without limitation the ownership and maintenance of certain common areas by a community
association formed for that purpose.

 E. Declarant intends that the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, assessments, charges, and liens
set forth below shall run with the land and be binding upon all persons or entities having or acquiring any right,
title, or interest in the Property or any portion thereof, and shall inure to the benefit of each Owner thereof.
F. Declarant has caused this Declaration to be prepared by Adrienne Vogel, Esq., of Vogel & Marsh LLP,
outside counsel to Declarant, in the manner set forth herein.
NOW, THEREFORE, Declarant hereby declares that the Property shall be held, sold, conveyed, encumbered,
hypothecated, leased, used, occupied, and improved subject to the following covenants, conditions, restrictions,
easements, assessments, charges, and liens, all of which are declared to be in furtherance of a general plan
and scheme for the subdivision, improvement, and sale of the Property.

ARTICLE II. DEFINITIONS
The following capitalized terms, when used in this Declaration, shall have the meanings set forth in this Article II.
Terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings customarily ascribed to them under Chapter 116 of
the Nevada Revised Statutes.
Section 2.1. "Articles." The Articles of Incorporation of the Association, as the same may be amended from
time to time.
Section 2.2. "Association." Desert Sage Ranch Community Association, a Nevada nonprofit corporation,
being the community association formed by Declarant to administer, own, and maintain the Common Area and
to enforce the terms of this Declaration. The Association is the community association contemplated by NRS
Chapter 116. All references herein to "HOA" mean the Association.
Section 2.3. "Board." The Board of Directors of the Association.
Section 2.4. "Bylaws." The Bylaws of the Association, as the same may be amended from time to time.
Section 2.5. "Common Area." All real property (including any Improvements thereon) that is (i) owned by the
Association in fee simple, or (ii) held by the Association under an easement, license, or maintenance obligation
for the common use and enjoyment of the Owners. Common Area expressly includes, without limitation, the
Common-Area Park, the Streetscape Common Area, the Entry Feature, and all landscaping, irrigation
infrastructure, hardscape, walls, monumentation, signage, and amenities located therein as installed by
Declarant or its successors. Common Area does not include any Lot or any portion of a public right-of-way
conveyed by dedication to Clark County or another public body.
Section 2.6. "Common-Area Park." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as
Parcel A, being an active-use park parcel improved with landscaping, irrigation, and, as installed by Declarant,
any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed, may consist of slides, swings, and climbing
structures). Parcel A is owned by the Association and is not part of any Lot.
Section 2.7. "Declarant." Callaway Land Partners, a Nevada limited liability company, and its successors and
assigns to whom the rights of Declarant hereunder are expressly assigned in a recorded instrument.
Section 2.8. "Declaration." This Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Desert Sage
Ranch, together with all exhibits and attachments hereto and all amendments and supplements duly recorded.

 Section 2.9. "Entry Feature." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as Parcel C,
being the community entry treatment situated at the intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, and
improved with entry monumentation, signage, walls, planting, irrigation, and accent lighting. Parcel C is owned
by the Association and is not part of any Lot.
Section 2.10. "Governing Documents." This Declaration, the Articles, the Bylaws, and the rules and
regulations of the Association, each as the same may be amended from time to time, together with all recorded
exhibits, plats, and supplemental declarations.
Section 2.11. "Improvement." Any structure, wall, fence, monument, sign, tree, shrub, turf, planting, irrigation
line, playground amenity, path, hardscape, or other tangible thing installed upon or affixed to the land.
Section 2.12. "Lot." Each numbered residential lot depicted upon a recorded final map of the Property and
intended for the construction and occupancy of a single detached residential dwelling. Each Lot is a separately
conveyable parcel; no Lot includes any portion of any Common Area, and no Common Area is any part of any
Lot.
Section 2.13. "Managing Agent." The community management firm engaged by the Association pursuant to a
written management agreement to perform the day-to-day administration of the Association's affairs, including
the maintenance and replacement obligations set forth in Article V. As of the date of this Declaration, the
Managing Agent is Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company, having offices
at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120.
Section 2.14. "Map" or "Final Map." Any final subdivision map of any portion of the Property recorded in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder, including the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, recorded at Book
175, Page 60) and any successive final map for Phase 3.
Section 2.15. "Owner." The record holder of fee simple title to a Lot, excluding any person or entity holding title
solely as security for the performance of an obligation.
Section 2.16. "Property." All of the real property described in Article III below and shown upon the Map(s),
together with all Improvements thereon, and any additional property annexed hereto in accordance with this
Declaration.
Section 2.17. "Streetscape Common Area." Those parcels or strips of Common Area situated between the
back-of-curb of a public street and the front or side lot lines of the adjoining Lots (or, where applicable, between
the back-of-curb and a perimeter community wall), extending along all frontage of the Property, and improved
with sidewalks (where the sidewalk is not within the dedicated public right-of-way), desert planting, street trees,
and drip irrigation. Each Streetscape Common Area parcel is owned by the Association and is not part of any
Lot.

ARTICLE III. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION
Section 3.1. Legal Description of the Property. The Property subject to this Declaration is that certain real
property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark County, State of Nevada, more particularly described as
follows:
A portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County, Nevada,
containing approximately 140.0 acres, together with all easements, tenements, hereditaments, and
appurtenances thereunto belonging, commonly known as Desert Sage Ranch, situated at the
intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las Vegas, Nevada 89178.

 Section 3.2. Phasing. The Property is subject to development in three sequential phases:

rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

Procedure Handout — Land Development Applications

CLARK COUNTY, NEVADA
500 S. Grand Central Parkway · Las Vegas, NV

MAP AMENDMENT AND VACATION PROCEDURES
Amended Final Maps · Vacation and Abandonment · Realignment within Project Design
At a glance. A recorded final map is a public record. The dedications, easements, and property lines
shown on it may only be modified through one of three routes: Amended Final Map, Vacation and
Abandonment, or an internal Realignment that does not touch a recorded right. Choose the correct route
at the start of the project to avoid duplicate submittals and lost recordation dates.

1. PURPOSE
This handout summarizes the routes available in Clark County for altering rights, easements, dedications, boundary
lines, lot configurations, or other features that appear on a subdivision map already recorded with the Clark County
Recorder. It is issued jointly by the Clark County Department of Public Works (Development Review and the Office
of the County Surveyor) and the Clark County Department of Comprehensive Planning as evergreen guidance for
owners, engineers, surveyors, and their counsel.
A recorded final map is a public record. The dedications, easements, and property lines shown on it may only be
modified through one of the procedures below. Choosing the correct route at the start of a project avoids duplicate
submittals, wasted review cycles, and lost recordation dates.
The three routes are:
• Amended Final Map — for corrections and modifications that keep the subdivision in place but revise

recorded easements, lot lines, or map features. Utility rights are relinquished and re-granted on the amended plat
itself.
• Vacation and Abandonment — for the elimination of previously dedicated public rights (streets, alleys,

drainage easements, or portions thereof). The action is legislative and requires public hearings.
• Realignment within the applicant's own project design — an in-house design change that does not touch any

recorded right or dedication. No County land action is required, but revised plan sheets and an additional plan
check cycle are.
Applicants unsure which route applies should schedule a pre-application conference with the Office of the County
Surveyor before preparing exhibits.

2. AMENDED FINAL MAP
An Amended Final Map is used to revise a recorded final map without extinguishing the underlying subdivision.
Typical uses include:
• Correcting scrivener's errors or bearing/distance ties disclosed after recordation.
• Adjusting interior lot lines between adjoining lots under common ownership.
• Relocating, widening, narrowing, or vacating and re-granting private utility easements.
• Adding easements not shown on the original recorded map (for example, a public utility easement needed to

serve a later phase).
Clark County · Department of Public Works · Department of Comprehensive Planning
Evergreen procedural guidance — verify current forms and fees at intake.

Page 1

Clark County · Public Works · Comprehensive Planning

• Modifying private street or common-area boundaries within the subdivision.

The Amended Final Map is prepared on the Clark County Amended Final Map form. Applicants must use the
current form; earlier versions will be rejected at intake.

2.1 Form Layout and Key Characteristics
(a) Certificate sheet. The certificate sheet of the Amended Final Map reproduces the entire certificate set from the
original recorded map — Owner's Certificate and Dedication, Nevada notary acknowledgment, Utility/Agency
Approvals, Surveyor's Certificate, County Surveyor's Certificate, Zoning Approval, Division of Water Resources
approval, and Southern Nevada Health District certificate — updated for the current signatories, together with an
additional OWNER'S CERTIFICATE OF AMENDMENT executed by the current fee owner(s). The Certificate
of Amendment recites the recording reference (book and page) of the map being amended and identifies, by short
description, what is being changed on each affected sheet.
(b) Utility Relinquishment Block. A dedicated utility relinquishment block is provided on the amended final map
form. In this block the named utility companies whose easements appear on the recorded plats being amended
formally relinquish their rights in those easements in favor of the easements granted (or re-granted) on the new
amended plat. Each named utility executes the block through its authorized right-of-way representative. Where an
easement is being reduced, relocated, or reconfigured, the relinquishment operates concurrently with the new grant
on the same instrument, so that at no point is the utility left without a recorded easement over its facilities.
The utility relinquishment block replaces separate quitclaims and quitclaim deeds for the affected easements. This is
the operative feature of the amended final map route: the map itself is the instrument of both surrender and re-grant.
(c) Other map elements. The Amended Final Map otherwise retains the standard Clark County final map elements
— title block identifying the subdivision, section/township/range, and M.D.M.; vicinity map; basis of bearings
statement; Recorder's note citing N.R.S. 278.5695; and filing block with book and page for the amended recording.

2.2 Submittal and Review
Amended Final Map submittals follow the current Public Works submittal guidelines. The package is filed with the
Office of the County Surveyor for technical review. In parallel with the County Surveyor's technical review, the
applicant is responsible for circulating the mylar or its digital equivalent to each named utility to obtain the required
signatures in the utility relinquishment block.
Required items at submittal:
• One completed Amended Final Map Application form.
• Amended Final Map mylars (or approved digital submittal) on the current County form.
• Original recorded final map with the sheets being amended clearly indexed.
• Updated title report (or title update endorsement) dated within thirty (30) days of submittal, disclosing current

fee ownership and any recorded encumbrances affecting the area being amended. Signatures on the Owner's
Certificate of Amendment must correspond to the vesting shown in the updated title report.
• Legal descriptions of any easements being relinquished or granted.
• Closure calculations for revised boundaries.
• Traverse and boundary files in the format specified by the County Surveyor.
• Executed relinquishment/consent letters from any beneficiary whose interest is not covered by the utility

relinquishment block (for example, private easement holders of record).
• Fees per the current fee schedule.

Clark County · Department of Public Works · Department of Comprehensive Planning
Evergreen procedural guidance — verify current forms and fees at intake.

Page 2

 Map Amendment and Vacation Procedures

Clark County · Public Works · Comprehensive Planning

The County Surveyor reviews for form, mathematical closure, correspondence with the original recorded map,
adequacy of the Certificate of Amendment, and completeness of the utility relinquishment block. Comments are
returned to the applicant's surveyor of record for correction. Utility signatures are gathered in parallel with technical
review so that mylars are ready for recordation as soon as County review clears.

2.3 Typical Processing Time
5 weeks to recordation from a complete submittal, assuming (i) a first submittal that meets the checklist, (ii) all
utility signatures returned within the same period, and (iii) title update and ownership signatures in hand at first
submittal. Incomplete submittals, holds for utility responses, and title updates that must be pulled during review are
the most common causes of schedule slip.
